articles.summary: The University of Florida filed a notice of intent to hire an H-1B visa holder as a financial analyst for a salary of $64,928.The employment period as
articles.body: The University of Florida filed a notice of intent to hire an H-1B visa holder as a financial analyst for a salary of $64,928.The employment period as mentioned in the notice is from February 2, 2027, to February 1, 2030. A notice of intent is not a job posting; it is strictly regulatory compliance to inform current employees that the employer (here, the university) has filed a Labor Condition Application to hire an H-1B. Generally, a candidate is already selected for the position when the notice of intent is published.While the filing came at a time when H-1B hiring across the US is under watch, Florida has already stopped H-1 B hiring in universities earlier this year.University president Stuart Bell said the filing was made without his approval and has been removed immediately. The university is following the statewide ban on H-1B hiring that the Florida Board of Governors voted for on March 2 and will be in effect until January 5, 2027. In the vote, it was decided that universities won't have to fire existing H-1Bs and their contract can be renewed too but there will be no new hiring of H-1B visa holders.“This job was posted without my approval or authorization, and it has been removed," Bell said. "The University of Florida will continue to remain in full compliance with Governor DeSantis’ direction on H-1B hires.”The filing came to light when Chris Brunet, a former contributing editor at The American Conservative who now runs an online newsletter, posted the details on X.The University of Florida employs the largest number of H-1B visa holders among the state’s public universities, according to The Independent Florida Alligator.Florida Guv Ron DeSantis' war against H-1BIn October 2025, DeSantis questioned why universities had staff members on H-1B visas such as a public-policy professor from China, a psychologist and counselor from the United Kingdom, an athletics operations and communications coordinator from Trinidad and Tobago and an assistant swimming coach from Spain. He was speaking at the University of South Florida. "We can do it with our residents in Florida or with Americans, and if we can't do it, then, man, we need to really look deeply at what is going on with this situation," DeSantis said.By January 2026, the Florida Board of Governors set up a proposed ban on H-1Bs for final approval. The voting took place in March and the ban is in place.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: BHOPAL: A man allegedly killed his wife at their home in Gwalior on Thursday morning following a domestic dispute. Police said Anand strangled Madhu Srivastava and then repeatedly struck her on the head with a pestle used for crushing spices at their home in Tyagi Nagar, near Defence School, under Murar police station limits.Madhu, who was observing the Karwa Chauth fast for her husband's long life, died on the spot. The couple are in their early 40s.Anand called the police himself and reportedly told them he would open the door only after they arrived. Local resident Akash Rana, who lives near the couple's house, said police called him and he accompanied them while they searched for the house.Anand remained in phone contact with the police throughout. When Rana entered the house with the police, Madhu was already dead. Police took Anand into custody and are questioning him.The motive remains unclear. Police and a forensic science laboratory (FSL) team collected evidence from the scene. The cause of death and the exact circumstances of the assault will be established through the post-mortem and forensic findings.Investigators are also examining whether there had been earlier signs of domestic discord.The couple married for love in 2010 and have a son and a daughter. Both children were reportedly at home at the time, along with Madhu's sister-in-law, who was in another room.Family members said they did not hear any screams, and police are examining these accounts.Some neighbours described Anand as unemployed and said he frequently shouted at home. articles.title: A century later, World War bombs still haunt Europe as Italy finds 250 munitions in melting glaciers
articles.summary: More than a century after the First World War, melting glaciers in Italy's Dolomites are exposing a deadly reminder of the conflict, with the Italian Army
articles.body: More than a century after the First World War, melting glaciers in Italy's Dolomites are exposing a deadly reminder of the conflict, with the Italian Army recovering around 250 unexploded munitions from the mountains.The discovery is part of a wider European problem, where shells, grenades and aerial bombs left behind by the First and Second World Wars continue to emerge from glaciers, forests, farmland and urban construction sites.According to CNN, the Italian Army's Julia Alpine Brigade recovered and neutralised the munitions during a clearance operation that ended on October 16. The weapons date back to the White War, fought between Italian and Austro-Hungarian forces in the Alps from 1915 to 1918, when soldiers battled in some of Europe's harshest mountain terrain.The recovered ammunition included Italian artillery shells and French-made Thevetot mortar bombs, alongside other unexploded devices.The first find of the summer was a 90-millimetre mortar shell discovered in June near Caldonazzo after a car rolled down a ravine. The army’s specialist bomb-disposal team subsequently removed it, while the wider clearance operation involved working at high altitudes and across difficult mountain terrain, according to CNN.The danger is not confined to Italy's melting glaciers. Across Europe, unexploded ammunition from both world wars continues to surface decades after the fighting ended, with drought, falling river levels, construction work and wildfires revealing weapons that had remained buried or submerged.In Belgium, the annual discovery of First World War ammunition in former battlefields is so common that the practice of finding remnants while ploughing fields is known as the “iron harvest”.The country's explosive ordnance disposal service responds to more than 3,000 calls a year and disposes of 200 to 250 tonnes of munitions left over from both world wars, according to the Associated Press.Germany faces a continuing challenge from unexploded Second World War aerial bombs, many of which are discovered during construction and infrastructure projects. In March 2026, authorities in Dresden defused a 250-kilogram British bomb found during work near a bridge in the city centre, evacuating around 18,000 people before the operation.France has faced a similar problem after wildfires swept through the country's southwest in August 2026. In Le Porge, near Bordeaux, bomb-disposal specialists recovered more than 400 shells and other munitions believed to date from the Second World War.The cache included French and German mortar shells, as well as other ammunition. Authorities said the heat had caused some buried shells to explode, alerting them to the hidden weapons.The discoveries underline how Europe's wartime legacy remains a present-day hazard more than 80 years after the Second World War and over a century after the First.From Alpine glaciers to former battlefields and urban construction sites, unexploded shells and bombs continue to surface, with changing environmental conditions making some of these long-hidden dangers harder to predict.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Turn the blade inward': Xi swings the axe again, expels 33 in major CCP purge
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping has intensified his sweeping anti-corruption campaign, with the Communist Party expelling 33 members, including senior
articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping has intensified his sweeping anti-corruption campaign, with the Communist Party expelling 33 members, including senior military officers and prominent political figures, as a key leadership meeting exposed the scale of the ongoing purge.The expulsions were confirmed in a communique issued on Thursday at the end of a four-day, closed-door meeting of the Communist Party's Central Committee in Beijing. Sixteen of those expelled were from the military, according to the BBC, as party discipline and political loyalty took centre stage at the gathering.Xi urged the Communist Party and the military to “turn the blade inward”, launch a self-revolution and root out “viruses” undermining their institutional health.The fifth plenum of the current Central Committee was marked by an unprecedented number of absences in the post-Mao era. Only 279 members attended, compared with 315 at the previous plenum in October 2025 and 364 in July 2024. The committee, which began its term in 2022 with more than 370 members, has been steadily depleted by Xi's crackdown.The party cited "serious disciplinary and legal violations" in its announcements, without providing details of the specific allegations against the officials.Xi, who came to power in 2012, has made combating corruption a defining feature of his leadership. However, analysts say the campaign has increasingly become a means of enforcing political obedience and consolidating his authority, with even officials handpicked for senior positions failing to escape scrutiny.Military purge leaves top ranks depletedAmong those expelled were former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui, former senior generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli, and prominent diplomat Liu Jianchao. Zhang Youxia was a vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission (CMC), the body responsible for overseeing China's armed forces, while Ma and Zhang were former members of the powerful Politburo.The latest action follows the removal of former general He Weidong and other senior military figures in an earlier round of expulsions. The continuing purge has raised questions about the leadership and operational readiness of the People's Liberation Army (PLA), even as China showcases advances in its military capabilities.The CMC has been reduced to just two members: Xi, its chairman, and Zhang Shengmin, its vice-chairman. The party elevated Zhang to the 24-member Politburo during the plenum, making him the only military representative on the top governing body.The party also adopted a resolution calling for stricter internal discipline, stronger anti-corruption enforcement and greater ideological purity. According to state news agency Xinhua, the leadership said it must strengthen its long-term governing capacity and maintain close ties with the people.The BBC reported that China's top anti-corruption watchdog had disciplined 680,000 people across the party apparatus in the first nine months of this year. The latest expulsions bring the number of members removed during Xi's third term to 51, compared with 35 in his first term and five in his second.Amidst the purge, Zhang Shengmin, vice chair of the Central Military Commission, was promoted to the ruling Communist Party’s Politburo.The 68-year-old veteran military official rose to become China’s second-highest-ranking general last year, during the fourth plenum.Xi tightens grip ahead of 2027 leadership reshuffleThe timing of the crackdown is significant, with the next Communist Party Congress scheduled for the second half of 2027. The gathering will determine the party's next leadership line-up, and Xi is widely expected to seek a fourth term, extending his rule beyond the decade-long limit followed by his predecessors.The scale of the purge suggests that the leadership is scrutinising officials more closely ahead of the reshuffle. Xi has repeatedly warned against cadres who profess loyalty but fail to follow party directives, reinforcing the view that political allegiance is central to the campaign.Chong Ja Ian, a non-resident scholar with Carnegie China, told the BBC that the anti-corruption drive had increasingly become an effort to consolidate and maintain authority, rather than simply address graft.The crackdown has also extended beyond the party and military. Reports cited by The Economist have highlighted the detention or disappearance of business executives and figures linked to strategically important industries, raising concerns about the consequences for China's business climate.You use AI every day. articles.title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements
articles.summary: Tourism and business leaders have been reacting to John Healey's first Budget as chancellor.
articles.body:
Tourism and hospitality leaders have been reacting to this week's Budget.

Among the headlines in chancellor John Healey's first Budget on Wednesday were a £100 payment to help millions of households with energy bills, a VAT cut on electricity bills and a freeze on fuel duty, both extended to July.

It also announced Devon would get an elected mayor in 2028 white Cornwall was included as the only area on a pathway to become a Foundation Strategic Authority.

Sue Jewell, chair of South East Cornwall Tourism Association and a holiday accommodation provider, said the budget "gave with one hand and took with the other".

As part of the Budget legal minimum wage is to rise by 3.9% in April

Jewell said: "I think it's tricky because actually I would believe that quite a lot of people in our business anyway pay over the minimum wage just to retain staff.

"However because of the cost we've cut back on staff.

"Which is sad really because it's local people who could be having local jobs."

Dr Harry Pitts, senior lecturer in Politics at the University of Exeter's Cornwall Campus, said the £100 energy payment was one of the "small things to make life a little easier for some households in the immediate period".

Anyone living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment", funded by extra tax on banks.

The Budget announced the threshold at which high street shops start paying business rates in England was to be increased from £12,000 to £18,000, meaning businesses would pay no rates on properties with a rateable value below this level.

Toby Parkins, interim ceo at the Cornwall Chamber of Commerce, said he predicted this would benefit about 900 extra businesses in Cornwall.

"For the small business that is a big win," he said.

Helen Wylde-Archibald, from the Devon Chamber of Commerce, said she "welcomed some stability".

"The last two have been a bit scary for business," she said, referring to previous Budgets.

She added: "It doesn't necessarily give us all the conditions we want for full growth and strong growth, but the main thing was there was no broad base business tax rises and fuel duty remains frozen until July."

She said she didn't think there was enough in the way of announcements of more support for farming and food, and this had "an impact on the rural economy".

James Kittow, from Butcher & Grazier in Cornwall, said: "It just seems like we've been forgotten again.

"We're an industry that is ready, willing and able to help the country produce the food for the nation."

He added there was no change on inheritance tax for farmers. Since April, inherited farming assets worth more than £2.5m face 20% inheritance tax

"I'm looking to plan for a succession... we want to keep farming, we want to keep doing what we love doing but if we're going to get hit on the other end of it then it does make you think twice about what is all this for, and it's just so sad for the future farmers that want to come into the trade," he said.

Andrea Drew, managing director at Lander Mortgage Services, said the key announcement relating to housing was a scheme for first time buyers, and a a "First Time Buyer Isa".

This is an account in which savers can build up a deposit, with the government topping up contributions of up to £4,000 each year with a 25% bonus.

"The only negative I would say... on new builds, the housing market isn't just all about new builds, it's about existing property... because not everybody wants to have a new build property," she said.

She added: "The other thing was about the increase in tax for landlords so, they're increasing the tax by 4%."

She said she'd seen landlords who decided to sell their property because of the amount of tax but tenants couldn't afford to buy the homes.

"What tenants need is more homes to choose from, not fewer, and they can't solve the housing shortage by destroying people who are providing the housing," she said.

articles.title: ‘Canada cannot be an EU member because of geography’: Von der Leyen proposes associate membership for Ottawa
articles.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed a new partnership between the European Union and Canada.
articles.body: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed a new partnership between the European Union and Canada. The proposal involves an associate membership status that would bring Ottawa closer to the bloc without granting it full membership.According to Reuters, von der Leyen said the EU was discussing the possibility of Canada becoming the bloc’s first associate member from outside Europe. She described the proposed arrangement as “association without accession”, saying it would bring the two sides closer than any partnership the EU had established before.“Canada cannot be an EU member because of geography, but we want to take our relationship to the highest possible level,” von der Leyen said.She added that associate membership would be reserved for the EU’s closest partners outside Europe, with the arrangement aimed at aligning policies more closely while stopping short of full membership.The development comes as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to diversify the country's trade ties and reduce its dependence on the United States amid escalating trade tensions with President Donald Trump.Ottawa has been looking to strengthen economic and strategic ties with Europe, particularly in areas such as critical minerals, artificial intelligence, energy and defence, while opening up new markets for Canadian businesses.Von der Leyen said the EU and Canada would seek to establish a “single space for strategic supply chains”, with both sides pursuing joint or complementary investments, including private financing.The proposed cooperation aims to strengthen economic links and secure access to strategically important materials as both sides seek to reduce supply chain vulnerabilities.She also said the two sides would work together to develop rules and standards for artificial intelligence, an area where closer regulatory coordination could strengthen their influence over global technology governance.Von der Leyen further announced that the EU and Canada would finalise an agreement the following day to bring Canada into Europe's supercomputing infrastructure. Such cooperation could support scientific research, advanced computing and AI development by improving collaboration between European and Canadian researchers.On security, von der Leyen said the two sides needed to adjust their strategic posture in the Arctic to defend their shared values.The region has gained geopolitical importance because of its natural resources, emerging maritime routes and strategic position, increasing the need for closer coordination among Western partnersYou use AI every day. articles.title: In 1905, a mine manager in South Africa pulled a 3,106-carat rough diamond from a mine wall; it became the Cullinan, cut into the 530-carat Great Star of Africa that now sits in the British royal sceptre
articles.summary: A glint on a mine wall in South Africa led to the discovery of one of the most celebrated diamonds in history.
articles.body: A glint on a mine wall in South Africa led to the discovery of one of the most celebrated diamonds in history. On January 26, 1905, Frederick Wells, the surface manager of the Premier Mine near Pretoria, spotted a large crystal embedded in the rock and prised it out with his pocket knife. What initially appeared to be an unusual find turned out to be a 3,106-carat rough diamond, later named the Cullinan. More than a century later, its largest polished stone, the 530.2-carat Great Star of Africa, remains set in Britain's Sovereign's Sceptre with Cross, one of the most recognisable objects in the Crown Jewels.According to the Royal Collection Trust, the uncut diamond measured approximately 10.1 cm long, 6.35 cm wide and 5.9 cm deep. Its exceptional size, clarity and blue-white appearance made it an extraordinary discovery. It remains the largest gem-quality rough diamond ever found, according to the Historic Royal Palaces, which manages the Tower of London's historic site and its display of the Crown Jewels.A discovery that stunned the mining worldWells reportedly spotted the crystal while inspecting the mine, about 18 feet below the surrounding ground surface. He extracted it from the rock and took it to the mine office, where its unusual size quickly attracted attention. The diamond was named after Sir Thomas Cullinan, the chairman of the Premier Diamond Mining Company and the man associated with establishing the mine. The discovery attracted widespread public interest, with the enormous stone briefly displayed in Johannesburg before being sent to London in 1905.Its size presented an unusual problem: finding a buyer willing to pay for such a valuable and conspicuous gemstone. The stone remained unsold for a period before the Transvaal government purchased it and decided to present it to Britain's King Edward VII. The gift had political significance as well as monetary value. The Transvaal government presented the diamond to Edward VII in 1907, following the South African Wars of 1899-1902. The gesture was intended to help repair relations between Britain and South Africa after the conflict.A royal gift and an extraordinary journeyTransporting a diamond of such importance required elaborate precautions. Historic Royal Palaces records that a replica, guarded by detectives, was sent to London by ship, while the genuine diamond was dispatched through ordinary parcel post in an insured package. The unusual arrangement reflected concerns about the security of the stone during its journey. Despite the elaborate decoy operation, the diamond arrived safely.King Edward VII subsequently entrusted the stone to the Asscher firm in Amsterdam, then among the leading diamond-cutting specialists. Transforming the enormous rough crystal into polished gemstones required careful planning because a mistake could destroy an irreplaceable stone. The Royal Collection Trust records that the cutting process took eight months. Three men worked for approximately 14 hours a day to produce nine large stones, identified by Roman numerals from I to IX, along with 97 smaller brilliant-cut diamonds and unpolished fragments.The first blow broke the knifeThe cutting operation became part of the diamond's enduring legend. According to the Royal Collection Trust, workers spent four days preparing a groove for the cleaving knife. When the first blow was struck, the knife broke while the diamond remained intact. The subsequent attempt successfully split the stone, allowing the cutters to continue their painstaking work. The operation required an understanding of the diamond's internal structure, as the direction of cleavage determined how the rough crystal could be divided.The resulting nine major stones differed in shape and size. The largest became Cullinan I, also known as the Great Star of Africa, while the second-largest became Cullinan II, or the Lesser Star of Africa. Cullinan I weighs 530.2 carats. It is a large, pear-shaped brilliant-cut diamond and remains one of the most famous stones in the British royal collection.From rough crystal to the royal sceptreAfter Edward VII's death in 1910, his successor, George V, had Cullinan I incorporated into the Sovereign's Sceptre with Cross. Cullinan II was placed in the Imperial State Crown. The sceptre itself predates the diamond by centuries. Historic Royal Palaces notes that the Sovereign's Sceptre with Cross has been used at every coronation since the ceremony of Charles II in 1661. The addition of Cullinan I transformed the object into an especially striking piece of royal regalia.The two largest diamonds remain part of the Crown Jewels, displayed at the Tower of London. Other stones cut from the original crystal eventually became part of royal jewellery. Cullinan III and IV, for instance, have been used in royal ornaments, while other smaller stones were distributed through different arrangements.The original rough diamond therefore did not survive as a single gemstone. Instead, it became a collection of stones with distinct histories and settings, two of which acquired prominent roles in Britain's ceremonial monarchy.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Don't push us': SC warns of harsh stand on firecrackers if orders go unenforced
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday said it was not inclined to impose a complete ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, but warned authorities against
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday said it was not inclined to impose a complete ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, but warned authorities against pushing it to take a "very harsh stand" by failing to enforce its orders on the ground.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale said repeated judicial directions would serve little purpose unless authorities ensured compliance, stressing that air pollution affected "every living being"."We are not inclined to completely ban but don’t push us to take a very harsh stand," the bench said as reported by news agency PTI. The Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati outlined measures taken by the Delhi government and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to tackle pollution.“There is no point in passing orders and directions unless you give effect to them on the ground, otherwise, it becomes a mockery,” the bench observed.The court said the matter was not adversarial and called for serious action and cooperation from all stakeholders to regulate the use of firecrackers.“Every year we are trying to balance it out but unless there is cooperation from everyone, it can’t be done,” the bench said, adding that the concerned officers must be present on the ground to monitor implementation.The bench also suggested roping in prominent personalities, including sportspersons, to spread public awareness about the harmful effects of firecrackers.Bhati told the court that the Delhi government had drawn up an extensive plan to tackle the pollution season. Measures scheduled to come into effect from November include curbs on older vehicles and construction and demolition activities, along with staggered office timings.The Centre informed the court that internal consultations on the use of barium in firecrackers were still under way. Bhati sought three weeks to complete the process, and the bench said it would consider the issue after that period.The Supreme Court was hearing two petitions, including a suo motu case on air pollution in the National Capital Region covering firecrackers, stubble burning and solid waste management. articles.title: Nine of 14 plans for council overhaul withdrawn following review
articles.summary: Proposals to merge smaller councils to form larger unitary authorities were put on hold last month.
articles.body:
The government has announced further delays to nine of 14 major council mergers, with only five now going ahead.

Proposals for 14 regions to undergo mergers of smaller councils to form larger unitary authorities was put on hold by Local Government Secretary Angela Rayner last month, following concerns around legal challenges.

Local Government Minister Jim McMahon has told MPs the review had found the government's decision-making to be "robust", but nine areas have now been withdrawn for further review.

Only five of the original 14 regions will be taken forward, after three more weeks of consultation. Shadow local government secretary Katie Lam condemned the latest news as "a farce".

Mergers will continue to progress in East Sussex, Gloucestershire, Oxfordshire , Warwickshire and Worcestershire .

But the government is seeking "legal clarity" in the remaining nine areas, which are: Derbyshire , Devon , Hertfordshire , Kent, Lancashire, Leicestershire , Lincolnshire , Nottinghamshire , and Staffordshire.

In a Commons statement, McMahon said the government was "withdrawing the decisions announced in July" for those nine areas.

"I want to be absolutely clear that this is not a reflection of the work underpinning those proposals," he added.

The review will now focus on the nine areas where current plans have been withdrawn for further review, as well as four areas where plans were withdrawn in September, in Essex , Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk.

Two further areas, Cambridgeshire and West Sussex, are still waiting for merger plans to be agreed, totalling 15 regions where local government reorganisation plans remain undecided.

McMahon said: "We will move faster where we can, and some of the remaining areas may receive an outcome decision before others.

"I commit to coming back to the House with updates for another set of areas by Christmas, and every area will have an outcome by early next year."

Reconfirming local elections in May 2027 would go ahead on existing council boundaries, he announced plans for elections to shadow councils, set to run for a year before taking over from old authorities, will now be held in May 2028.

Responding, Lam set out how the reorganisation had been beset by delays over the past two-and-a-half years.

"From start to finish this government's approach to local government reorganisation has been nothing short of a farce," she told MPs.

She added: "Naturally the taxpayer was left to pick up the tab for all of these delays - a bill which runs into the tens of millions of pounds."

Local Government Association chair Eamonn O'Brien called for a re-set of relations between the government and local councils across the country.

He said: "While today's announcement provides some certainty for some areas, many councils remain frustrated by the situation they have been placed in.

"All councils affected need urgent clarity on next steps and how costs already incurred will be met.

"There needs to be a reset in the relationship between government and councils on local government reorganisation, with local government fully engaged in shaping decisions from the outset."

articles.title: Germany, South Korea enhance strategic, security ties against backdrop of China-Russia-North Korea collusive threat
articles.summary: SEOUL: Ahead of the 19th Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business here in the South Korean capital, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz held a summit with
articles.body: SEOUL: Ahead of the 19th Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business here in the South Korean capital, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz held a summit with South Korea’s President Lee Jae-myung, setting out a roadmap for an enhanced security partnership and raising their overall bilateral relationship to an Enhanced Strategic Partnership.Both sides agreed to deepen their ties in security and defence through regular military exchanges, training cooperation, and to conclude a bilateral agreement on the protection of classified military information. President Lee also expressed the interest of Korean defence companies in forming long-term partnerships with Germany, including through joint ventures and joint development projects.The summit and the Asia-Pacific Conference comes against the backdrop of Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine that has seen more than 10,000 North Korean soldiers participate in that war on Russia’s behalf. This has raised serious concerns in Seoul that North Korean soldiers have gained high-tech battlefield experience that could now be deployed by Pyongyang on the Korean Peninsula.Meanwhile, China’s domination of global supply chains has allowed Beijing to provide industrial support to Russia and help it evade sanctions, thereby keeping Moscow’s war machinery going. Chancellor Merz, who has been on a week-long tour of East Asia with stopovers in Singapore and Japan, has been critical of this China-Russia collusion. In Singapore, Merz demanded that Beijing use its influence over Moscow to ensure a just peace in Ukraine, and called for strengthening economic relations between Europe and the Indo-Pacific region to reduce one-sided dependence on China.The wars in Ukraine and Iran, and China’s fingerprints on both conflict theatres, have sharply brought home the point that Europe’s economic and security interests are intertwined with that of Asia’s. And it is this reality that is compelling German businesses, as represented in the Asia-Pacific Conference, to look for resilient supply chains, non-hegemonic partnerships in critical technologies like AI, semiconductors and batteries, and cultivate suitable leverage against China’s weaponisation of its industrial domination.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump official reacts to leaked video of Microsoft's AI chief telling staff company wants to bring foreign talents: 'You were hoping we were kidding'
articles.summary: Anthony D'Esposito, the inspector general of the Department of Labor, once again targeted Microsoft after he chose to share a video of a Microsoft boss
articles.body: Anthony D'Esposito, the inspector general of the Department of Labor, once again targeted Microsoft after he chose to share a video of a Microsoft boss explaining to his staff the Green Card situation of the company. Microsoft's Green Card program has been suspended by the administration, which accused the company of Green Card abuse. The company denied the allegations. In his internal question-and-answer session, Scott Guthrie, the executive vice president of the Cloud and AI group at Microsoft, said the company wants to bring more talent into the United States."On the most recent announcements, we are working with the US administration to get clarity because we said publicly that...I encourage you to see Brad Smith's comments...you know that we are not sure that everyone's looked at the right data...with some of the comments that were made last month. And we are working to share what we see in the data and explain things... the most important thing is that we work with the individuals. Because every individual that's on a visa or has applied for a visa or a Green Card, everyone's situation is slightly different. It's super important that we take care of the people," Guthrie said adding that if someone has been impacted, they should reach out to HR.What Microsoft said after Green Card suspensionMicrosoft said the company has a rigorous process for PERM jobs and they did not violate any rule."We believe in the strength and talent of the American workforce. That is why the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans."We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. These were not to hire new people. The remaining filings for new employees were for individuals already legally in the United States who decided to come work for us, and they equal only 1% of our U.S. workforce. They are not new arrivals to our country."Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the rigorous standards of this visa category. We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work."Microsoft succeeds as a global technology leader by developing the world’s best technology workforce. We do this by strengthening this country’s talent pipeline, hiring American workers, and attracting the best talent from around the world."What did Brad Smith say?Microsoft vice chair and president Brad Smith said the Trump administration's move sent across a wrong message. “I think we should all be worried about sending — intentionally or inadvertently or otherwise — signals that send the most talented next wave of AI [or] SI software engineers to other countries, rather than the United States,” he said adding that Vice President JD Vance did not have the right data about Microsoft's Green Card sponsorships.'Don't screw American workers'D'Esposito reacted to Guthrie's internal message about seeking clarity and doubled down on the fact that the administration has been very clear. "Don’t screw American workers. Don’t use visa programs as a back door into our nation. We were clear. You were hoping we were kidding. We’re not," he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Spain train tragedy: Glitch, 3 operator errors behind crash that killed 68
articles.summary: A technical glitch followed by a series of alleged human errors at a railway control centre may have led to a devastating collision between two high-speed
articles.body: A technical glitch followed by a series of alleged human errors at a railway control centre may have led to a devastating collision between two high-speed trains in Spain, killing 68.According to Spanish news outlet El Diario, the incident began around 8.30am on Wednesday when a computer malfunction knocked out the LZB train control system on a 69-km stretch of track. The failure automatically stopped several trains, including an Iryo service and a state-owned Renfe AVE train travelling behind it.However, instead of requiring the AVE train to proceed at a restricted speed, the control centre at Madrid's Atocha station allegedly instructed its driver to resume the journey at normal speed. The train was travelling at high speed when it struck the stationary Iryo train from behind at around 8.53am near Urda, in central Spain.El Diario, citing audio recordings of conversations between train drivers and the control centre, reported that the operator appeared to have authorised the resumption of services without applying the necessary safety precautions. The recordings raised questions about whether the operator had misread the relevant protocol and failed to account for the position of the Iryo train.When the LZB system is unavailable, railway procedures require trains to operate under trackside signalling, with drivers proceeding at sight speed. According to El Diario, industry sources said this means travelling at no more than 40 kmph, allowing drivers to react to obstructions ahead. A high-speed train travelling at around 200 kmph, by contrast, can require more than a kilometre to stop.The report also highlighted a second missed opportunity to prevent the collision. About five minutes after the AVE train was authorised to resume its journey, the Iryo driver contacted the control centre to report that her train remained stopped because of the signalling problem. She was also told to continue at normal speed once able to do so.Despite the communication, there was no indication in the recordings that the control centre warned the AVE driver about the stationary train ahead. The AVE travelled approximately 25 km before the collision.Transport minister Óscar Puente described the decision to allow the AVE train to resume at normal speed as “inexplicable”. The investigation by the Civil Guard and Spain's Railway Accident Investigation Commission is expected to establish how the technical failure and decisions at the control centre contributed to the disaster.The crash is Spain's second deadly high-speed rail accident this year, following a January collision that killed 46 people. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has pledged a full investigation and improvements to restore public confidence in the country's rail network.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Netanyahu's unity government gambit: Can he lure Eisenkot from  opposition?
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is exploring ways to form a national unity government with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot following the October
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is exploring ways to form a national unity government with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot following the October 27 election. Meanwhile, Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman also appears to be distancing himself from the opposition bloc and favouring a unity arrangement, according to reports published in The Jerusalem Post and Maariv.According to the report, sources close to Netanyahu are reportedly promoting a plan to bring Eisenkot into a government led by the Likud chief, despite Eisenkot's pledge not to serve under him. Meanwhile, N12 News reported on Wednesday that Liberman had cut off contact with Eisenkot and former prime minister Naftali Bennett, and had stopped answering calls from his opposition counterparts.The developments come as the Central Elections Committee continues to update the results. Its final report is not expected to be submitted to the president until next week. Netanyahu's ability to form a government will depend on the final seat count and whether he can secure support beyond his existing bloc.Netanyahu camp explores power-sharing dealNetanyahu declared in his speech at the Jerusalem International Convention Center that "We must establish a strong national right-wing government." However, sources close to him began briefing reporters that same night on a possible unity government involving Eisenkot.According to the sources, Likud officials believe Eisenkot has few viable alternatives. They argue that the opposition bloc has exhausted its electoral potential, including among Israelis who travelled from abroad to vote. They also believe the high turnout in the Arab sector would be difficult to replicate in another election.The officials say Israelis living abroad are unlikely to purchase expensive plane tickets to vote again just a few months later.Sources close to Netanyahu claim that "Eisenkot will not survive another round and may even lose his position as head of the bloc."They believe Eisenkot could eventually agree to join a Netanyahu-led government despite his previous commitments. However, the reports do not indicate that Eisenkot has agreed to consider the proposal.Two possible arrangements under discussionThe briefings from Netanyahu's circle have outlined different versions of a possible agreement.Under one proposal, Netanyahu would offer Eisenkot the second half of the prime ministerial term under a rotation arrangement. Likud officials say Netanyahu would remain in office until the end of US President Donald Trump's term, "finish the job in Iran", and lead regional peace initiatives before handing over the premiership to Eisenkot after about two years.Under another version, Netanyahu would refuse to agree to a rotation and instead offer Eisenkot a senior ministerial portfolio.The proposed framework would initially bring together Netanyahu, Eisenkot, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, without the ultra-Orthodox parties.According to Likud figures promoting the plan, the ultra-Orthodox parties want to resolve the military conscription issue. However, their rabbis fear that public and political responsibility for legislation allowing ultra-Orthodox men to be drafted into the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) would fall on them.Under the proposal, the government would first pass the conscription law without the ultra-Orthodox parties participating in the coalition. Those parties could then join the government after the legislation is approved, expanding its support.Netanyahu's associates believe the arrangement could give Eisenkot a significant achievement on military conscription and persuade him to join the government.Opposition rejects prospect of Eisenkot joining NetanyahuEisenkot has previously pledged not to serve under Netanyahu, and political figures remain sceptical about the proposed arrangement.Sources in the opposition bloc have categorically rejected the possibility of Eisenkot joining a Netanyahu-led government, describing such a move as "complete suicide, both morally and politically".Some political figures, including those on the Right, argue that joining Netanyahu at this stage could end Eisenkot's political career. They also question whether pressure from President Isaac Herzog or Trump would change his position.They point to the precedent of Benny Gantz agreeing to a rotation arrangement with Netanyahu only after three rounds of elections, amid the coronavirus crisis and growing public frustration over political deadlock.The political climate has since changed, these figures argue. Opposition voters are reportedly more willing to lift the boycott of Arab parties than to accept a government with Netanyahu and his political partners.They also question why Eisenkot would need to join the coalition if a security escalation with Iran occurred. He could instead follow Liberman's approach after October 7 and support the government from outside the coalition without formally joining it."As long as his voters oppose joining Netanyahu, Eisenkot will not go against their wishes," political sources estimate.Liberman cuts contact with opposition leadersIn a separate development, N12 News reported on Wednesday that Liberman had cut off contact with Eisenkot and Bennett and had not answered calls from opposition counterparts since the day after the election.Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu party is currently projected to win seven Knesset seats, below pre-election polls that had suggested it could secure as many as nine.According to N12, Liberman lost ground to Bennett, whose B'Yachad party absorbed some of his mandates. His election strategy had also relied on Likud fracturing internally, but official results show the party retaining its position as the largest faction in the Knesset.Liberman had launched his campaign with the ambition of becoming prime minister, but fell short. Despite his reported shift towards a unity government, he has remained adamant in his refusal to join Netanyahu's coalition.His opposition to Netanyahu was also evident in his recent call for Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara to open a criminal investigation into the prime minister. Liberman alleged that Netanyahu had attempted to draw the IDF into a military confrontation to delay the election.According to N12, Liberman does not intend to be the one to cross over to Netanyahu's bloc and allegedly prefers that Eisenkot do so alone.Sources close to Liberman told N12 that he is "choosing to lie in wait", as a security escalation could create further opportunities for political realignment.Netanyahu's options depend on final resultsNetanyahu's associates believe recruiting opposition lawmakers could become a simpler route to forming a government if his bloc approaches 60 Knesset seats. Likud officials claim they have already identified potential candidates who could be persuaded to cross political lines.However, the final results remain pending, and there is no indication that Eisenkot is prepared to join Netanyahu or accept either proposed arrangement.The central question is whether Netanyahu can secure enough support to govern without relying solely on his existing right-wing and ultra-Orthodox allies. The opposition, meanwhile, faces the challenge of maintaining unity as leaders reassess their options following the election.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2022, conservators X-raying a Van Gogh painting in Edinburgh found a hidden self-portrait of the artist on the back of the canvas, concealed for more than a century under layers of glue and cardboard
articles.summary: \"How can I be useful, of what service can I be? There is something inside me, what can it be?\" Van Gogh said.
articles.body: "How can I be useful, of what service can I be? There is something inside me, what can it be?" Van Gogh said. Although the quote referred to the internal world, the news coming from the National Galleries of Scotland is proving it true for his art as well. Whenever we talk about art, among the few pictures that come to mind is the beautiful Starry Night by the famous Vincent van Gogh. So much so that it has now become a part of pop culture. You can see Van Gogh-inspired art everywhere, from tote bags to T-shirts. The once lesser-known artist has become the embodiment of omnipresence.Do you know that a few years ago, in 2022, experts at the National Galleries of Scotland found a centuries-old, previously unknown self-portrait of the artist? Before the commencement of an exhibition, conservators were examining the canvas using X-rays when a hidden portrait was discovered. The self-portrait, concealed for more than a hundred years, was covered by layers of glue and cardboard on the back of an earlier work called Head of a Peasant Woman.All the members, including senior conservator Lesley Stevenson, were shocked to find the artist's eyes looking back at them.Van Gogh lived a humble life; his work did not sell during his lifetime, and the craze for his art came only after his death in 1890, at the age of 37. Due to poverty, the artist often reused canvases to save money, mostly by turning them over and working on the other side. Who knew that the once-unknown artist would become the face of Western art history?What did the X-ray reveal about the hidden portrait?Sometimes, what we are looking for outside is sitting right next to us. The exclusive painting was not found at another exhibition or auction; it was discovered during a routine check of Head of a Peasant Woman, painted in 1885. Conservators at the National Galleries of Scotland were examining the artwork as part of a cataloguing exercise ahead of the exhibition A Taste for Impressionism when the X-ray images revealed the face hidden on the reverse side of the canvas.The image showed a bearded man wearing a brimmed hat and a loosely tied neckerchief, staring directly at the viewer. One side of his face appeared in shadow, while his left ear was clearly visible. The intense gaze and recognisable features helped experts identify the figure as Van Gogh himself. What makes the discovery particularly interesting is that the portrait had remained concealed even though the painting had been part of the gallery's collection for decades.Why was the self-portrait covered up?As mentioned earlier, Van Gogh had a habit of reusing canvases due to extreme poverty. The layers of glue and cardboard covering the portrait were believed to have been added in the early twentieth century, possibly when the painting was being prepared for an exhibition. They concealed the image on the reverse, leaving it hidden for more than a hundred years, away from the eyes of viewers.The habit of reusing canvases was not limited to this painting. He created several works on the reverse sides of earlier canvases, particularly during periods when money and art supplies were limited. The National Galleries of Scotland noted that other examples of double-sided paintings by the artist exist in collections around the world, including the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam.The discovery therefore adds to an already known aspect of his working life. Instead of treating the canvas as a surface that could be used only once, Van Gogh sometimes turned it around and began again. In this case, the decision left behind an unexpected second work, one that remained out of sight long after the artist's death.What happened to the hidden portrait?While the X-ray allowed experts and art lovers to view the portrait, uncovering the original painting was a much more complicated task. The layers of glue and cardboard had been attached to the canvas for decades, and removing them without damaging the delicate paint beneath required extensive conservation work.The challenge was to reveal the portrait without harming either artwork. Head of a Peasant Woman itself is an important work, and any attempt to remove the backing would have to account for the condition of both paintings. Conservators therefore had to investigate whether the materials could be separated safely before proceeding.In the meantime, visitors to the 2022 exhibition A Taste for Impressionism at the Royal Scottish Academy in Edinburgh could see the hidden portrait through an illuminated display of its X-ray image. It offered a rare opportunity to look at a painting that had remained concealed for more than a century, without disturbing the original canvas.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Steven Spielberg bought a 2.8-acre Los Angeles horse ranch for $5.75 million in 1999 and proposed a five-storey riding centre; after listing it for $29.9 million in September, the property has disappeared from listings
articles.summary: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg has pulled his Los Angeles ranch off the market after listing it for $29.9 million last month, Realtor.com reported.
articles.body: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg has pulled his Los Angeles ranch off the market after listing it for $29.9 million last month, Realtor.com reported. For nearly 27 years, Steven Spielberg, 79, and Kate Capshaw, 72, held a 2.8-acre property in Sullivan Canyon, Los Angeles, though they never lived there. The land was for the horses, and the couple’s plans for it were far bigger than a stable and a paddock.They bought the ranch in 1999Spielberg and his wife bought the estate in 1999 for $5.75 million. The property, now known as Dogwood, spans two parcels and sits in one of the city’s quieter canyons. Soon after the purchase, they began planning a major overhaul. They wanted to incorporate a five-storey riding facility, a guesthouse and a three-storey guardhouse, with a renovation budget of more than $7 million. Few homeowners in Los Angeles would take on a project like that, and fewer would attempt it in a residential canyon. Not everyone was happy with the scale of the plan. Many residents objected to the project’s size, and the criticism grew loud enough to slow it down. In January 2001, the couple withdrew their permit application, according to the LA Times. Their representatives said they would consider the residents’ concerns before going ahead. Later, the plan was scaled back to an outdoor riding ring. They dropped the covered structure that had drawn the most complaints.A ranch with horsesArchitect Michael Kovac, interior designer Michael Smith and landscape designer Christine London worked on the property. It now features a 20,000-square-foot riding arena. The main house, known as Dogwood, has seven bedrooms and 9.5 bathrooms. The property offers an impressive array of equestrian amenities alongside its luxurious living spaces. The couple listed the property for $29.9 million with Sandro Dazzan of The Agency.“Nestled in the ultra-private Sullivan Canyon, Dogwood is Los Angeles’ premiere equestrian ranch – a rare masterpiece designed by renowned architect Michael Kovac with interiors by Michael Smith and landscape design by Christine London,” the listing says.The main house leans into warmth. Walnut floors and wood-covered ceilings give the rooms a rich, rustic feel, while large windows fill them with natural light. The living room has several seating areas arranged around two fireplaces, making it suitable for quiet evenings and larger gatherings alike. That same natural look carries into the chef’s kitchen, with extensive wood cabinetry, an oversized centre island, high-end appliances and an eat-in nook. “The chef’s kitchen with eat-in dining nook and wood-burning fireplace connects to a cozy family room and IPE-clad terrace overlooking a tranquil reflection pond,” the listing describes. The kitchen opens onto a cosy family room and an IPE-clad terrace overlooking a tranquil reflection pond. Upstairs, the primary suite has its own wood-burning fireplace and a private covered terrace. Downstairs, a media room doubles as a games room, and a wine cellar rounds out the interior.The setup puts the horses at the centre of the property. Guests would notice the stables and the arena before the living spaces, the reverse of what one would expect at most Los Angeles estates.The couple used Dogwood as a private retreat for their horses rather than as a home.In September, when the couple put the property up for sale, they asked $29.9 million, roughly five times what Spielberg and Capshaw paid nearly three decades ago. Their plan to offload the property seems to have been put on hold, as property records now reveal that the home is off the market, the outlet confirmed.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Florida mom arrested for leaving 4 kids alone during 5-day Las Vegas work trip
articles.summary: A Florida mother accused of leaving her four children home alone during a five-day work trip to Las Vegas left them unsupervised for around 16 hours a
articles.body: A Florida mother accused of leaving her four children home alone during a five-day work trip to Las Vegas left them unsupervised for around 16 hours a day, while their babysitter lived about two hours away, police said.Irene Miller, 50, is facing four counts of child neglect after authorities said she left her children, aged 9, 11, 12 and 14, at their home in Kissimmee while she travelled to Las Vegas on October 18.According to the Osceola County Sheriff's Office, a babysitter hired by Miller would drop the children at school around 8 am and return at 4 pm after they came home. However, the caretaker did not stay overnight and lived near Tampa, around two hours away, leaving the children without adult supervision for much of the day and night.Police also found that although the house was clean and well maintained, there was relatively little food in the refrigerator for the four children.9-year-old injured by falling dumbbellThe alleged neglect came to light on October 21, when the children's 11-year-old sister and 12-year-old brother called 911 after their youngest sibling was injured by a falling dumbbell.The 9-year-old boy was building a fort using sheets and blankets when he reportedly used a dumbbell to secure a sheet to a piece of furniture. When he pulled the sheet, the weight fell and struck his forehead, according to Capt Kim Montes of the Osceola County Sheriff's Office. The injury required hospital treatment, where the cut was closed with medical glue.The eldest child, 14, was outside riding his bicycle when the accident happened. He returned after noticing emergency vehicles outside the home, authorities said.Deputies called Miller, who allegedly told them she was working in Las Vegas and was dismissive during the conversation.Montes said Miller subsequently called her eldest son and questioned him for contacting emergency services.“She’s berating the son for calling 911…while he was standing right there with the deputy. It was on speaker,” Montes told the New York Post.The captain said Miller did not return home immediately, even after learning that her youngest child had been taken to hospital.Mother arrested at airportAuthorities said Miller was returning from Las Vegas on October 23 when detectives met her at Orlando International Airport. She was interviewed before being arrested on four counts of child neglect without great bodily harm, according to the sheriff's office.She was booked into jail and later released after posting a $4,000 surety bond. Her next court date was not immediately clear.The children were placed in the care of their father, Mark Miller, 53, who was arrested in August over an alleged domestic battery incident involving his wife. He has pleaded not guilty to the charge.Court documents cited by the New York Post said Irene Miller had filed for divorce the previous month. The couple had been married for 15 years.The sheriff's office said the children could stay with their father despite a court-ordered no-contact order between the parents.“The Osceola County Sheriff's Office will not tolerate child neglect. These cases will be investigated, and charges will be brought against the parents who are not properly supervising or caring for their children,” Sheriff Chris Blackmon said in a statement.You use AI every day. articles.title: Houthis hold 37 UN food workers as Trump-backed WFP chief inherits humanitarian crises across globe
articles.summary: Luke Lindberg says 37 World Food Programme employees are detained by Houthis in Yemen, with some separated from families for nearly two years.
articles.body: Thirty-seven United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) workers are being held captive by Iran-backed Houthi terrorists in Yemen, the agency's new executive director told Fox News Digital on Wednesday. Many have been detained for two years. Luke J. Lindberg's remarks come as WFP workers face growing threats in some of the world's most dangerous conflict zones, where hundreds have died risking their lives to save others, he said. "Right now in Yemen, we have 37 colleagues of ours who are currently detained," Lindberg said. IRAN-BACKED TERROR PROXY HOUTHIS THREATEN FRESH ATTACKS AFTER YEMEN AIRPORT STRIKE "These folks are out there to provide basic humanitarian services. They're not there to influence the political outcomes of a conflict. And so we need to protect them, and we need to get our detained colleagues released." "All detainees are Yemeni nationals employed locally by the WFP, Lindberg clarified, before stating that some have been separated from their families for "nearly two years," he clarified. "It's a really complex political environment," Lindberg continued before adding that there are no current Americans in that pool. "They are all locally employed Yemenis," he clarified. Just three days into his tenure, Lindberg raised the detentions with U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz, underscoring the urgency of securing the workers' release. "Ambassador Waltz is aware, and the State Department team has done a great job of taking this seriously and also, it's a priority for them as it is for us to get these folks released." TRUMP OFFICIALS UNVEIL PRIVATE SECTOR BLUEPRINT FOR LIFE AFTER USAID "It's been almost two years," Lindberg said. "Away from their families. It breaks my heart." The detentions come amid Yemen’s crippling civil war between the internationally recognized government and Iran-backed Houthis, which has devastated the economy and left millions dependent on humanitarian aid. More than 18 million people face acute food insecurity, including more than two million children under age five suffering from acute malnutrition. "Our team operates in the most impossible and challenging conditions you can imagine around the world," Lindberg said. "People like me, we're not out in the field, literally handing food to people and literally cooking food for people so that they get the nourishment. It's the wonderful people, the people that choose to go out and do this work that are the real heroes of this equation." Lindberg said the WFP must now balance reaching vulnerable populations with protecting employees from unacceptable risks. "And so there are areas where we will go into, areas where you can't go into. Again, the goal is the end of the conflict and allow humanitarian resources to flow into those areas. "And until that happens, there are areas where we do not operate so that our staff can remain protected and that they can do their job safely." US VISA CLASH EXPOSES SUDAN’S FORGOTTEN WAR AS FOREIGN POWERS COMPETE FOR STRATEGIC FOOTHOLD The dangers extend beyond Yemen, with Lindberg saying conflict drives roughly two-thirds of acute food insecurity worldwide, with an estimated 266 million people facing severe hunger. "It means the most challenging levels of hunger we can imagine," Lindberg said. The crisis has intensified pressure on humanitarian organizations to deliver food in some of the world's most dangerous and inaccessible regions. "But the World Food Programme really has a great team operating in over 120 countries around the world, doing this hard work each and every day," he explained. Among the most urgent crises, he said, are those in Sudan, South Sudan and Somalia, where conflict, displacement and climate-related disasters have pushed vulnerable communities toward famine. Fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces has displaced millions and triggered famine conditions in parts of the country, with Lindberg saying Sudan will be his first field destination as executive director, reflecting the urgency of the crisis. "Right now, we are approaching famine levels in three countries, predominantly in the Africa region, in Sudan, South Sudan and Somalia," he said. "And so those are flash points for me that are incredibly important for us to focus on, find the resources that should be available to help us meet those needs specifically." Other humanitarian emergencies include Gaza, where fighting, damaged infrastructure, restricted access and funding shortages have complicated food deliveries, and Haiti, where gang violence has disrupted aid access. SAUDI ARABIA ON EDGE: ICONIC KINGDOM CENTRE SENDS WORKERS HOME AMID HOUTHI ATTACKS In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, fighting involving armed groups has displaced millions, while the war in Ukraine has also disrupted agricultural production and global food supply chains. But Lindberg said one of the most disturbing consequences of these conflicts is the rising death toll among humanitarian workers with hundreds killed worldwide in recent years. "Unfortunately, in the past couple of years, we've lost over 700 humanitarians around the world in their active duty. "To me, that's the worst possible outcome. It's really unacceptable. And so yes, many of our World Food Programme colleagues have unfortunately been caught up in those circumstances as well. "It's my commitment to call each one of those family members should that happen, but it's primarily my goal to not let that happen anymore." Lindberg's appointment comes as the WFP confronts major humanitarian emergencies and funding pressures, while also bringing the agency a direct connection to President Donald Trump. A South Dakota native, Lindberg previously served as undersecretary of agriculture for trade and foreign agricultural affairs at the U.S. Department of Agriculture, overseeing international agricultural assistance programs, including the McGovern-Dole Food for Education and Food for Progress programs. Lindberg succeeds Cindy McCain, who stepped down this year, with Deputy Executive Director Carl Skau serving in the interim. Since 1992, six executive directors were American. SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres and Food and Agriculture Organization Director-General Qu Dongyu appointed Lindberg after consulting the WFP Executive Board. Lindberg said Trump personally called to ask him to serve as the U.S. nominee for the position, a conversation he described as evidence of the president's commitment to humanitarian efforts. "When I was nominated to lead the World Food Program by the United States, President Trump personally took the time to call me and offer me this opportunity," Lindberg said. "And to me, that shows his heart for this work. He is somebody that believes in peace around the world. And for me to have the opportunity to speak with him about how the World Food Programme can. "To play an important role alongside the U.S. in addressing these humanitarian needs was a special moment that I'll never forget." That said, Lindberg is adamant that his new job at the World Food Programme comes with a clear mission: "show up no matter what." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP That means focusing on delivering food to those who need it, regardless of the politics involved. "To safely and effectively deliver food, and to really stay out of the politics of it, our goal is to feed hungry people." Fox News Digital's Sydney Finver contributed to this report.

articles.title: What caused the deadly train crash in Spain? What we know so far
articles.summary: Spain has begun three days of national mourning after 69 people were killed and over 100 injured in a high-speed train collision, the third deadly incident t...
articles.body:
Spain has begun three days of national mourning after 69 people were killed and over 100 injured in a high-speed train collision, the third deadly incident this year on the country's rail network.

The deadly crash happened Wednesday after one train plowed into another near the town of Urda, in Toledo province, on the high-speed line that connects Madrid and Seville. Authorities say the incident was caused by both computer system failure and apparent human error.

One of the trains, operated by Spain's national rail company Renfe, crashed into a stationary train operated by the private company Iryo, at a time when all rail traffic in the area was disrupted due to a problem with the LZB train management safety system.

The incident follows a major crash in January in Córdoba province in which more than 40 people died, and a crash near Barcelona that killed a train driver.

Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced an official mourning period from Thursday until Saturday. "All of Spain is in mourning," he said from the site of the crash as emergency work continued.

Spain's transportation minister, Óscar Puente, said that a computer system failure led to an issue with the safety system along a 63-kilometer (40-mile) stretch of track causing all trains in the area to be stopped automatically.

At that point, the state-owned company that manages Spain's railways, ADIF, took manual command of the system and a decision was made to allow the high-speed Renfe train to continue southbound along the tracks despite a red light.

The Renfe train was authorized to proceed without any speed restrictions due to an erroneous order from a train controller. As a result, Puente said that between 8:36 a.m. and 8:52 a.m. local time, it resumed traveling at about 124 miles per hour, eventually colliding with the stationary Iryo train.

"There was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorized to proceed," the transportation minister said at a press conference on Wednesday. "It is a decision made under inexplicable circumstances."

Following Puente's comments, Spanish trade union CSIF called on the transport minister to resign, saying: "We demand that the Government respect the investigation and the presumption of innocence for the head of traffic at ADIF." CNN has approached Spain's transport ministry for comment.

Audio recordings published in Spanish media reveal conversations between the train drivers and the controller in the moments leading up to the crash. The recordings appear to show that the Renfe train was given clearance to move, with the controller telling it to continue onward at "normal operation."

In another recording, the driver of the Iryo train involved in the crash also receives the instruction to resume "normal operation." Minutes later the driver reports that she is unable to restart her train and it is currently not moving.

Passengers told CNN that the moment of the crash on Wednesday was "very chaotic," and people were immediately thrown out of their seats and on top of one another inside the carriages.

One surviving passenger said that three of the train cars in particular "were in terrible shape."

"One was on fire, in another there were people trapped and crying," said the passenger, who declined to give her name. "And then in the main one (impacted) – there were people buried under debris."

Among those who were killed, 24 were on the Renfe train, traveling from Madrid to Seville, and 44 were on the Iryo train, also going between Madrid and Seville.

In total there were 151 passengers on the Iryo train and 393 passengers on the Renfe train, according to the latest update from the regional government of Castilla and La Mancha.

Of the 110 injured people who were taken to the hospital, 60 have been released, according to the latest update from the regional government on Thursday morning.

Puente added that there will be a full investigation into the incident.

Sánchez said that "if there has been negligence, it will come to light. And if there have been failures in the safety system, they will be addressed with the utmost firmness."

Little is known at this stage regarding who the victims are. Identification efforts are ongoing while emergency staff continue to comb through the wrecked carriages at the crash site, where rescuers and cranes worked through the night under floodlights.

The Spanish Civil Guard announced that it has opened four offices in different Spanish cities to swiftly identify the victims of the crash. The Civil Guard said that the DNA of families is being gathered to aid this process. 67 missing persons reports have been filed in the wake of the accident, the force confirmed to CNN.

One mother, Rosario, told CNN she had provided DNA samples to help find her missing 32-year-old son, Francisco José, who was on board one of the trains. Rosario said her son had also been about to board one of the trains involved in the Adamuz crash in January, but eventually decided to buy a ticket for a later journey instead.

The Civil Guard announced that one of its own officers lost his life in Wednesday's crash. Naming the victim as José Manuel, the police force offered its "deepest condolences" to his family, friends, and colleagues. A former Spanish minister, Fátima Báñez, was also killed, her People's Party (PP) confirmed on Thursday.

In the wake of the crash more than 500 emergency personnel were deployed to assist with rescue operations, Spain's interior ministry said, as well as at least three helicopters and several drones.

Authorities removed passengers without serious injuries away from the scene by bus. The evacuated passengers included citizens of multiple nationalities, including Spain, Brazil and elsewhere, according to CNN's producer at the scene. The US State Department has said "several" Americans were injured in the train collision.

Forty-two foreign citizens from seven countries were involved in the crash, including at least one who died and seven who were injured, Reuters reported citing Spain's foreign ministry.

Speaking from the crash site on Thursday morning, Sánchez told reporters that emergency teams were focusing on recovering the bodies of those who had died in the disaster so that the victims could be identified.

Sánchez said that the Spanish government would provide compensation for families of the victims at a later stage.

Sánchez said on Wednesday that "it's clear that we have suffered two terrible tragedies involving high-speed rail in the same year," acknowledging the other major crash in Córdoba province that killed more than 40 people in January.

The crash on Wednesday happened about 130 miles from the site of the January train disaster near the town of Adamuz, along the same high-speed rail route that runs between Madrid and Seville.

However, the cause of the train crash earlier this year was markedly different. That collision involved one train derailing due to a break in the track and crossing onto an adjacent track, according to Spain's public broadcaster RTVE.

Prior to the Adamuz train disaster, Spain's train drivers' union, SEMAF, had raised concerns about high speeds causing vibrations and subsequent wear and tear along high-speed railway lines, a source from the union told CNN at the time.

Spain's train drivers held a pre-planned nationwide strike Thursday to call for stronger safety measures.

Speaking to reporters during the strike, SEMAF Secretary General Diego Martín called for a "rigorous and independent investigation" into the crash and criticized the leaking of audio from the control center as "alarming, disrespectful and irresponsible."

A third crash this year near Barcelona – which happened days after the Adamuz train disaster – involved a commuter train derailing on a day of heavy rainfall. That crash killed the driver and injuring dozens of passengers, according to the regional government of Catalonia at the time.

The successive incidents have raised concerns about Spain's railway infrastructure, computer systems and the maintenance of both.

But prior to this year, European Union statistics show that Spain's rail safety record was better than many other European countries.

In 2023, Spain had fewer than 1 railway deaths per one million inhabitants – giving it the best record in the EU at the time, according to a Eurostat report. Most railway deaths in the EU are a result of unauthorized people on the tracks, rather than incidents that kill passengers or staff inside the train, data shows.

Wednesday's fatal crash has sparked fresh criticism of Sánchez and the fallout from the disaster will likely impact his left-wing government just four weeks before national elections on November 29.

The incident has served to further erode public trust in Spain's railway infrastructure and creates another major setback for a government already marred by recent corruption scandals and the Ceuta mass migrant crossing crisis earlier this year.

Protests erupted in Madrid on Wednesday night, with people calling for the resignation of both Sánchez and Transportation Minister Puente.

Videos from the demonstrations showed some protesters holding signs saying "corruption kills" and "leave!" alongside images of Sánchez.

CNN's Sophie Tanno, Vasco Cotovio, Sol Amaya, Catherine Nicholls, Michael Rios, Billy Stockwell, Jack Guy, Pau Mosquera and Duarte Mendonca contributed to this report.
