articles.body: The counting of votes in Israel’s election has confirmed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud as the largest party in the next Knesset, but left his right-wing bloc short of a parliamentary majority.According to official figures released by Israel’s Central Elections Committee (CEC), cited by Jerusalem Post, Netanyahu’s bloc secured 53 seats, while the opposition bloc seeking to replace him won 48. The results leave both sides well short of the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset, with Arab parties emerging as crucial players after winning a combined 19 seats.The final tally, which included the remaining double-envelope ballots, confirmed Likud’s position as the largest party with 27 seats. United Torah Judaism and Otzma Yehudit won seven seats each, while Shas and the Religious Zionist Party secured six apiece. The results differed from several pre-election television polls, which had projected fewer seats for Likud and stronger performances by some of its allies.With neither camp able to command a majority on its own, attention will now turn to coalition-building efforts and the possibility of a minority or unity government.Israeli President Isaac Herzog is expected to consult party representatives after the formal publication of the final results before nominating a candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government. If the candidate fails, another leader could be given an opportunity. Failure to complete the process within the stipulated timeframe could eventually trigger another election.A unity government involving Likud and opposition parties such as Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar, Naftali Bennett’s Together faction and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beytenu could command 66 seats. However, such an arrangement appears unlikely at present, given the opposition’s campaign pledge to remove Netanyahu from power and his dependence on far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies.The Arab parties’ combined tally could also prove decisive if Eisenkot’s bloc attempts to form a minority government with their support from outside the coalition.The final count comes amid allegations of election interference and voter fraud. CEC chairman Noam Sohlberg asked Shin Bet chief David Zini to investigate suspicions that foreign entities may have attempted to influence voting in the Arab sector. articles.title: Map that came to symbolise America's divide over slavery auctioned for nearly $1 million
articles.summary: A hand-drawn map of the Mason-Dixon Line, which became a symbol of the divide between free and slave states in the United States, sold for $950,000 at an
articles.body: A hand-drawn map of the Mason-Dixon Line, which became a symbol of the divide between free and slave states in the United States, sold for $950,000 at an auction in Asheville, North Carolina, on Thursday. Forty-five bidders competed for the historic document, with the contest lasting just under three minutes.The bidding began at $400,000 for the survey, completed in 1768 by British surveyors Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon. The sale was conducted both online and in person at Brunk Auctions. Although the final price fell short of the auction house's high estimate of $1.2 million, its vice-president Lauren Brunk said she was pleased with the result.“It’s a very high price for a map," she said.The buyer has asked to remain anonymous, at least for now, Brunk said. The Library of Congress, which lost out when the map was sold in 1982, did not participate in Thursday's bidding.The map was originally commissioned to resolve a boundary dispute between the colonies of Maryland and Pennsylvania. However, its historical significance grew over time as the Mason-Dixon Line became associated with the division between the northern free states and the southern slave states.The line was later used in the 1820 Missouri Compromise to establish limits on slavery in the young United States. It became synonymous with the deep divisions over slavery that ultimately led to the American Civil War four decades later.The late publisher Malcolm Forbes bought the map in 1982 for $360,000, outbidding the Library of Congress. It was sold again in 2002 for $556,000, making Thursday's sale a significant increase over its previous auction price.Brunk said she was pleased that the historic document had been entrusted to the auction house.“I would like to say I’m thrilled that this is going to a good home and we are so happy to have had it in our presence for these last months,” Brunk said. “It also feels like a privilege to have been entrusted to steward this one owner to the next.”A vertical section of the map depicting the Delaware-Maryland border is housed at Princeton University.You use AI every day. articles.body: SRINAGAR: In a setback to J&K govt, the high court (HC) of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh Thursday struck down the 2010 Water Resources Act, ruling that water usage charges levied on hydropower projects amounted to a tax on electricity generation, a subject beyond the erstwhile state legislature’s powers.A division bench of Justices Sanjay Dhar and Rajnesh Oswal quashed demand notices issued to 13 independent power producers and restrained J&K govt from imposing any tax on electricity generation under the guise of water usage charges or any other levy.The producers had challenged the law, arguing that charges fixed by Water Resources Regulatory Authority on April 2, 2019, were linked to the height from which water drove turbines rather than the volume consumed, effectively taxing power generation.Govt defended the levy, citing its authority to regulate water storage and use, National Water Policy and the need to conserve J&K’s water resources.Rejecting its arguments, HC held that the legislation exceeded the erstwhile state’s legislative competence when enacted. articles.title: In 2017, a British food rescue organisation started with one person and a van collecting surplus food; nine years later, UKHarvest has rescued 10 million meals and now collects 10 tonnes of surplus food every week
articles.summary: If you have ever been to a supermarket, you will know that food often remains unsold even when it is perfectly good to eat.
articles.body: If you have ever been to a supermarket, you will know that food often remains unsold even when it is perfectly good to eat. A bag of carrots rejected because one is too crooked. A crate of apples set aside because of a small bruise. A loaf of bread left on the shelf because it is nearing its use-by date. Similarly, what happens to produce when a farmer cannot find enough buyers? Have you ever wondered what happens to all this food? Much of it risks ending up in the bin.For most of us, the story ends there. But in southern England, one woman saw an opportunity to change that. In 2017, Yvonne Thomson founded UKHarvest, inspired by the need to reduce food waste at a time when more people were struggling to afford food. What began as a one-person-and-a-van mission has since grown into a food rescue operation that has saved the equivalent of 10 million meals!From one van to a fleetThe first UKHarvest vehicle was a single van, and its base was a lock-up in Chichester, which doubled as a small storage unit for whatever food could be saved that week. The idea was simple: collect surplus food from farms and food businesses before it was thrown away, then get it to people who needed it. Initially, the work was mostly about moving food from one place to another. Over time, the charity learned that handing out food is only part of the job. People also need affordable options, and they often need to know what to do with what they receive. This need led to the expansion of its services into several strands. UKHarvest’s Community Food Hubs bring affordable food straight into local neighbourhoods, so families do not have to travel far to access it. Nourish Hub, which opened in West London in 2021, combines nutritious meals with food education. In 2024, another programme, a Grub Club, was launched. It caught the eye of local schools and now supports 20 primary schools in West Sussex. Children learn about food as well as eat it. A child who grows up understanding where dinner comes from is likely to make different choices later. In January 2026, the charity added Community Grub Clubs and a Nourish Hub Café to its list of services. Today, the charity runs a fleet of vans and a warehouse with chilled and frozen storage, which means it can keep a wider range of food safe for longer.The amount of surplus food the charity collects each week has now reached 10 tonnes, UKHarvest confirms. It sources this surplus food from growers, producers and distributors across the south of England and West London.Queen Camilla is the charity’s patron. “With the generous support of Queen Camilla as Patron, UKHarvest has continued to grow into an outstanding charity, delivering affordable food and free food education to thousands of people each year through our Community Food Hubs, Grub Clubs, Nourish Hub and community cafés. The team and volunteers work towards a more sustainable food system at a time when the cost of living continues to rise and more people are using our services, keeping the community at the centre of everything we do. Thank you,” Susannah Day, Chair of the Board of UKHarvest, said in a statement.The charity reached the 10 million meals milestone on Friday, 16 October, World Food Day. A delivery pushed the charity’s total to the equivalent of 10 million meals. UKHarvest is treating the figure as a starting point rather than a finish line. It is asking local residents, businesses and food producers to help shape what comes next.You can also contribute to the cause, either through a one-off or regular donation. You can also volunteer your time, while food producers and businesses can contact the charity about donating suitable surplus food. articles.title: PU finally sends job letter to Jyoti’s brother
articles.summary: Panjab University sends appointment letter to Jyoti’s brother after her death; family awaits receipt and demands action on inquiry findings and accountability.
articles.body: Chandigarh: Panjab University (PU) has dispatched an appointment letter to the younger brother of PhD scholar Jyoti for a job in the university, fulfilling an assurance made to the family after her death. However, the family is still awaiting the letter and says that providing employment alone is not enough, with accountability for the lapses identified in the magisterial inquiry also needing to translate into concrete action.Jyoti’s paternal uncle, Jitendra Kumar, said the family would decide its next course of action after receiving the appointment letter. “We are waiting for the letter. Once we receive it, we will act accordingly. But accountability is equally important. Something concrete should be done on the findings of the inquiry, and those responsible should be held accountable,” he said.A PU spokesperson confirmed that the appointment letter had been dispatched to the family.According to a university document dated July 28, following a meeting with Jyoti’s family on the day of her death, PU had agreed to offer her brother, Pawan Kumar, employment as an electrician. The document specified a pay scale of Rs 19,900 plus Rs 400 grade pay, along with dearness allowance and other allowances under Punjab govt rules, subject to the prescribed eligibility and procedural requirements.The appointment letter states that Pawan will be on probation. The family is awaiting the communication to confirm the appointment details and complete the joining formalities.The job was part of the assistance announced by the university after Jyoti’s death. The July 28 document also recorded financial assistance of Rs 5 lakh from the vice-chancellor’s discretionary fund and Rs 11 lakh through the office of the dean student welfare.The family’s demand for accountability comes after the Chandigarh deputy commissioner forwarded the magisterial inquiry report to the PU vice-chancellor on Oct 27. The DC asked the university to fix departmental responsibility on the sub-divisional engineer (electrical), junior engineer-in-charge, electrical inspector and other electrical maintenance staff concerned according to their assigned duties.The communication also called for departmental proceedings over lapses in inspection, maintenance, supervision and electrical safety management, an immediate electrical safety audit of the South Campus and priority rectification of identified defects.Jyoti, 28, was pursuing a PhD in microbiology and died near Girls Hostel No. 8 on PU’s South Campus while proceeding to her department on July 28.The family has questioned why two engineering officials suspended after her death were reinstated before the inquiry concluded. articles.title: Over 1cr to elect 3,626 sarpanch in second phase today
articles.summary: Over 1.06 crore voters in Rajasthan vote today to elect 3,626 sarpanch and 33,804 ward panch; polling 7am–6pm at 11,799 booths via ballot papers.
articles.body: Jaipur: More than 1.06 crore voters will cast their ballots Friday to elect 3,626 sarpanch and 33,804 ward panch across Rajasthan’s gram panchayats in the second phase of panchayat elections. While there are 21,839 candidates for sarpanch posts in the fray, 45 were elected unopposed.The nomination process, including scrutiny and withdrawal of candidature, was completed Thursday with election symbols allotted and the final list of candidates released the same day. Of the 1 crore voters, 55,19,336 are men and 51,36,744 are women. Polling will be held from 7am to 6pm, followed by counting immediately after voting, with results expected by late night.Meanwhile, Rajasthan recorded a final voter turnout of 65.1% Wednesday in the second phase of elections for zila parishad and panchayat samiti members across 124 panchayat samitis and 352 zila parishad wards.A total of 1,06,56,127 voters are eligible to exercise their franchise in the second phase. Polling will be conducted at 11,799 booths across the state.Unlike elections to zila parishads and panchayat samitis, voting for sarpanch and ward panch posts will be conducted through ballot papers, not electronic voting machines (EVMs). Each voter will cast two votes — one for a ward panch candidate and the other for a sarpanch candidate.The ballot papers will be prepared by the polling parties in the respective gram panchayats after the final list of candidates is released. There will be separate ballot papers for ward panch and sarpanch elections, with candidates’ names written by hand against their allotted election symbols.Jodhpur district will witness the highest number of elections in this phase, with voting for 442 sarpanch and 3,768 ward panch posts. articles.title: DNA mismatch leads to acquittal in schoolgirl rape case
articles.summary: Panchkula court acquits 23-year-old in Class X student rape case after DNA mismatch and contradictions; charges under POCSO Section 6 and IPC 376 fail.
articles.body: Panchkula: A Panchkula court has acquitted a 23-year-old man in a rape case involving a Class X student who gave birth in her govt school’s toilet in 2023, citing insufficient evidence and contradictions in the prosecution’s case.Acquitting the accused of charges under Section 6 of the POCSO Act and, alternatively, Section 376 IPC, the court observed that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. It noted that the evidence suffered from material contradictions and lacked the credibility required to sustain a conviction.The case came to light after the newborn’s body was recovered from a dustbin. The girl had allegedly disposed of the baby after presuming the infant was dead. She is also facing a separate case in connection with the incident.In her initial statement to police, the girl said she had been in a consensual relationship with the accused. However, in a subsequent statement, she alleged that the relationship was forced.A key factor in the acquittal was the DNA evidence. The accused’s DNA profile did not match either the girl or the baby. Tests, however, confirmed that the girl was the biological mother of the infant.Another accused in the case, the girl’s neighbour, was a minor at the time. Proceedings against him are pending before the Juvenile Justice Board.Defence counsel argued that his client had been falsely implicated and pointed to the DNA mismatch, inconsistencies in the girl’s statements and the lack of corroborative evidence. The court ultimately granted the accused the benefit of doubt.According to the prosecution, the complainant, whose identity has been withheld under the POCSO Act, initially stated that she had been in a consensual relationship with the accused since Aug 2022. She claimed she was unaware of her pregnancy and unexpectedly delivered a baby in the school washroom on May 15, 2023. Believing the infant showed no signs of life, she allegedly placed the baby in a dustbin.Based on her statement and the subsequent investigation, an FIR was registered at Chandimandir police station on May 20, 2023. The mother of girl later sought to have her statement re-recorded, following which she made fresh allegations. During the investigation, the minor neighbour was also named as an accused. Police said the minor admitted involvement in the incident, while the 23-year-old was later arrested from Chandigarh railway station.
